points.description: States FALSE (the statement is incorrect: the instruction set architecture IS an abstraction provided by the CPU to the OS).
Justification: the ISA is an abstraction in which instructions are mapped to functionality, and the ISA instructions plus registers are what the OS uses for its functionality.
Key point: the implementation details / how the functionality is achieved by the CPU are not known to the OS (hidden behind the ISA).
States that the OS understands/targets the ISA, so an OS needs to be compiled differently for different ISAs.

rubric.notes: Full marks need FALSE plus a precise justification covering all four elements: ISA as abstraction mapping instructions to functionality (with registers), implementation hidden from the OS, and OS compiled per ISA. Per the question, no correct justification means no marks, so a bare FALSE or TRUE earns 0. Vague or generic statements (e.g. 'OS uses the CPU') earn nothing; any wrong claim in a point voids that point.
